AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #17
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Livestock Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Livestock Nutrition.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Livestock Nutrition.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Livestock Nutrition.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Livestock Nutrition.

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Nitrogen gas only

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Health: Disease Control? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Health: Disease Control.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Health: Disease Control.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Health: Disease Control.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Health: Disease Control.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Erosion Control? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Erosion Control.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Erosion Control.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Erosion Control.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Erosion Control.

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Urban and peri-urban Agriculture? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.

7. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Powered Agricultural Implements? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Powered Agricultural Implements.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Powered Agricultural Implements.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Powered Agricultural Implements.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Powered Agricultural Implements.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Cropping? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Cropping.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Cropping.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Cropping.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Cropping.

11. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

13. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agri- business Accounts? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Agri- business Accounts.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agri- business Accounts.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agri- business Accounts.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agri- business Accounts.

15. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Forage Crops? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Forage Crops.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Forage Crops.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Forage Crops.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Forage Crops.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Urban and peri-urban Agriculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Powered Agricultural Implements and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Agricultural Biotechnology and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Agri- business Accounts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Business and Career Opportunities in Agriculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
